title: Singapore International Commercial Court (International Committee) Bill
what_it_is: Singapore International Commercial Court (International Committee) Bill

sections.label: SICC caseload and survey ranking
sections.summary: The SICC's caseload rose about 30% in 2023, with a substantial increase in fresh filings over two years, and it was voted the most used international commercial court globally in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Since its introduction, the SICC’s caseload increased by about 30% in 2023, with a substantial increase in fresh filings in the SICC over the past two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the SICC was voted the most used international commercial court globally in 2024 in the Singapore International Dispute Resolution Academy International Dispute Resolution Survey 2024.

sections.label: International Committee as standalone body
sections.summary: The International Committee will be a standalone body hearing prescribed civil appeals of an international and commercial nature from prescribed foreign courts, and will not be a court of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: First, the International Committee will be a standalone body hearing prescribed civil appeals of an international and commercial nature from prescribed foreign courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: While there will be strong linkages between the International Committee and Singapore’s judiciary, the International Committee will not be a court of Singapore, nor will it exercise the judicial power of Singapore.

sections.label: Minister for Law regulations powers
sections.summary: The Minister for Law will be empowered to make regulations on appealable case types, the International Committee's powers, and ancillary matters such as ad hoc member appointments and panel composition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Minister for Law will be empowered to make such regulations concerning the types of cases that can be appealed to the International Committee from a prescribed foreign jurisdiction, the powers of the International Committee and ancillary matters, such as the appointment of ad hoc members and the composition of the International Committee panel.

sections.label: Singapore and Bahrain sign Treaty
sections.summary: On 20 March 2024, Singapore and Bahrain signed a Treaty for Bahrain to establish the BICC and for Singapore to designate a body to hear appeals from the BICC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: On 20 March 2024, Singapore and Bahrain signed a Treaty for Bahrain to establish the Bahrain International Commercial Court (BICC) and for Singapore to designate a body to hear appeals from the BICC.

sections.label: Opt in or out appeals
sections.summary: Parties may agree to opt in or opt out of appeals to the International Committee depending on the BICC's jurisdiction, and the panel will have at least three members including one International Judge and one ad hoc member.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Broadly, depending on the nature of the BICC’s jurisdiction over the matter, parties may agree to "opt in" or "opt out" of appeals to the International Committee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: And the International Committee panel will consist of at least three members who include one International Judge and one ad hoc member.

sections.label: Bill establishes International Committee
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to establish the International Committee of the SICC, empowered to hear prescribed civil appeals and related proceedings from foreign jurisdictions, as a milestone in positioning Singapore as an international dispute resolution hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill represents an important milestone in our journey to position Singapore as a pre-eminent international dispute resolution hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It seeks to establish a new body, the International Committee of the SICC, which will be empowered to hear prescribed civil appeals and related proceedings from foreign jurisdictions.

sections.label: Minister for Law prescribes appealable cases
sections.summary: The Bill gives the Minister for Law power to prescribe which cases may be appealed from a foreign jurisdiction to the International Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, the Minister for Law will have the power to prescribe the types of cases that may be appealed from a foreign jurisdiction to the International Committee.

sections.label: Enforcement of International Committee judgments
sections.summary: The Bill treats an International Committee judgment or order as equivalent to one from the foreign jurisdiction where the appeal originated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, I commend the Bill’s provisions on enforcement, which treat a judgment or order of the International Committee as equivalent to a judgment or order of the court of the foreign jurisdiction from which the appeal originated.

sections.label: REFJA registration and Bahrain appeal mechanism
sections.summary: Judgments once registrable under RECJA are now registrable under REFJA, covering money and non-monetary judgments, and a May 2023 Bahrain MOU established an appeal mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Judgments that were once registrable under the RECJA are now registrable under the Reciprocal Enforcement of Foreign Judgments Act, or REFJA, which covers not only money judgments but also non-monetary judgments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is a progressive development that aligns with Singapore’s goal to make cross-border dispute resolution more efficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would also like to commend Singapore’s recent Memorandum of Understanding with Bahrain’s judiciary in May 2023, which established an appeal mechanism between the Bahrain International Commercial Court and the SICC.

sections.label: Singapore-China judicial cooperation MOU
sections.summary: On 1 April 2023 the Supreme Court signed an MOU with China's Supreme People's Court on managing international commercial disputes, particularly the Belt and Road Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On 1 April 2023, Singapore’s Supreme Court signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Supreme People’s Court of China, focusing on cooperation in managing international commercial disputes, particularly in relation to the Belt and Road Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This partnership also was discussed at the sixth Singapore-China Legal and Judicial Roundtable in February 2023, co-chaired by Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon and His Excellency Zhou Qiang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Strategic Roadmap for Judicial Cooperation that emerged from these talks provides a framework for Singapore-China collaboration in this arena.

sections.label: International Committee hears prescribed appeals
sections.summary: The International Committee will hear prescribed appeals of an international and commercial nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As mentioned in my speech, the International Committee will hear prescribed appeals of an international and commercial nature.

sections.label: Precedential value under foreign jurisdiction law
sections.summary: The precedential value and effect of International Committee judgments in the relevant foreign jurisdiction is subject to that jurisdiction's law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As judgments and orders of the International Committee are judgments and orders from the foreign jurisdiction which the relevant appeal arises from, their precedential value and effect in that particular jurisdiction, is subject to the law of that jurisdiction.

sections.label: International Committee judgment foreign court
sections.summary: An International Committee judgment is a judgment of the foreign court appealed from, and the Committee views public policy from that foreign jurisdiction's perspective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As pertinently observed by Mr Zhulkarnain, an International Committee judgment will be a judgment of the foreign court from which the appeal arose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is intended that the International Committee approach public policy considerations from the perspective of that foreign jurisdiction.

sections.label: Singapore exploring similar collaborations
sections.summary: Singapore is prepared to explore similar collaborations with other states, with each request negotiated and assessed individually, and must continue to innovate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Singapore is prepared to explore similar collaborations with other states.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Each request would have to be negotiated and assessed individually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: While Singapore has made remarkable progress in facilitating cross-border legal cooperation and shaping the future of global commercial justice, we must continue to innovate to continue on this path.
